meta.title: THE AI RISHI immersive research, second pass
meta.replaces: docs/immersive-web-research.json as the evidence set. v1 stays in the repo as the record of category playbooks.
method: Each lessonForTheAiRishi is written for this pass and names a decision for this product.
Observations come from public award notes, known production stacks, and the behavior of canonical products. They are not screenshots of all of these homepages taken in this session.

Rows that only existed to hit a category quota, and rows whose technique fields would have been a shared template, were dropped. If a URL was not actually known, the row was dropped instead of given a plausible sentence.
v1's Lando Norris heroTechnique was the sports template. The Lando row here uses the published stack and the frame-by-frame campaign, and rejects Taxi.js because it animates history.

sites.name: Lando Norris
sites.interaction: Scroll steps through frames of one campaign rather than hovering cards.
sites.motion: Pixel breakup, a drawn signature, and a race calendar are scrubbed, not faded.
sites.space: A helmet-scale WebGL object occupies the page; type is a layer on that film.
sites.storytelling: A season is the narrative. Fixtures are chapters.
sites.navigation: Watch, shop, and table stay reachable. Taxi.js also animates route changes.
sites.typography: Poster type, split on scroll, not a docs headline.
sites.technology: Webflow, GSAP, ScrollTrigger, SplitText, three.js, Rive, Lenis, Taxi.js — public stack writeups.
sites.performance: Film and WebGL together. Heavy on purpose. Not a model for a 120-day reader.
sites.mobile: The next fixture and the table have to work one-handed. The film can simplify.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Take 'the object is the page.' Do not take Taxi.js: it animates history, and back/forward must stay native.

sites.name: Active Theory
sites.interaction: Case studies behave like rooms you enter, not thumbnails you scan.
sites.motion: Theatre.js timelines direct one idea per piece. Motion is staged, not a kit of hovers.
sites.space: Custom WebGL environments. The portfolio is a sequence of worlds.
sites.storytelling: Each project has one concept. They do not stack effects to look busy.
sites.navigation: Work index is spatial. A normal header still exists so you can leave.
sites.typography: Type is set inside the world, subordinate to the idea.
sites.technology: Custom WebGL plus Theatre.js. Their own writing and FWA notes, not a scraped project DOM (that fetch returned no project HTML).
sites.performance: Large scenes, fallbacks when WebGL is declined. Budget we do not have.
sites.mobile: A lighter fallback is part of the craft, not an afterthought.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: One persistent world with one idea. Do not build a gallery of unrelated WebGL tricks.

sites.name: Lusion
sites.interaction: Scroll is the prompt ('scroll to explore'); the reel is optional, not autoplay-with-sound as the only path.
sites.motion: 3D sequences are the motion. The page keeps asking you to continue rather than revealing cards.
sites.space: Campaign worlds. Depth is the product they sell.
sites.storytelling: Featured work is a film strip of other people's brands, which is right for a studio and wrong for a school.
sites.navigation: About, work, and contact still resolve. The scroll line is flavor.
sites.typography: Short stacked lines ('Step into a new world') act as chapter titles.
sites.technology: In-house WebGL. Labs live at labs.lusion.co.
sites.performance: A studio reel is allowed to be heavy. A lesson is not.
sites.mobile: The mobile site still has to offer the work without the desktop camera path.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Material and camera sell 'alive' better than more meshes. Do not become a showreel of client films.

sites.name: Unseen Studio
sites.interaction: Brand systems (Illoca, Hubtown, OceanX) are interacted with as products, not as moodboards.
sites.motion: GSAP, ScrollTrigger, SplitText, CustomEase on Illoca — directed, not ambient.
sites.space: Three.js and SVG share one frame. Flat graphics and depth are one system.
sites.storytelling: A brand launch is the story. The site is the proof, not a case-study PDF.
sites.navigation: Vue-based product UI where the work is a tool (Illoca), not a hamburger maze.
sites.typography: Type is a brand asset that moves, then sits still to be read.
sites.technology: GSAP + Three.js + SVG + Vue, per Unseen's own Illoca note.
sites.performance: Award work (SOTD, developer awards) still has to load as a marketing site.
sites.mobile: Illoca is a product people use on a phone. Motion cannot be the only interface.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Directed motion plus a readable product. Our lesson pages are Illoca's quiet mode; the homepage is the launch.

sites.name: Immersive Garden
sites.interaction: Cartier, Omega, Aramco, and 100 Lost Species are played or scrolled as chapters.
sites.motion: Each campaign has its own tempo. There is no house fade they reuse on every brand.
sites.space: Full-frame narrative space. The product (a watch, a species) is in the room.
sites.storytelling: A luxury object or a cause is told once, thoroughly.
sites.navigation: Campaign microsites often hide the studio. The Awwwards profile is the index.
sites.typography: Fashion and editorial type, reset per brand.
sites.technology: Bespoke WebGL production. 3 SOTY, many developer awards. Studio URL is not asserted here because the reliable public index is the Awwwards profile.
sites.performance: Campaign budgets. We will not ship a 10MB film to say 'phase two'.
sites.mobile: A film that does not degrade becomes a poster. They design the poster too.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: One subject, told completely. Our subject is the 120-day path, not a watch.

sites.name: Resn
sites.interaction: Playful objects beg to be poked. Interaction is the joke and the craft.
sites.space: Toy-like 3D. The page is a place.
sites.navigation: You hunt for the next toy. That is a bad pattern for a curriculum.
sites.technology: Custom WebGL, historically Flash-era DNA, now WebGL.
sites.performance: Heavy loads are part of the show. We refuse a blocking boot.
sites.mobile: The toy often dies on a phone. A course cannot.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Personality without a mascot. No character, no long lock, no poke-the-lotus toy.

sites.name: Bruno Simon
sites.interaction: You drive. Keyboard is the primary pointer. Clicking is secondary.
sites.motion: The camera follows a vehicle. Idle is the world waiting.
sites.space: A literal small world: terrain, projects as buildings.
sites.storytelling: The portfolio is a trip. Projects are places you stop.
sites.navigation: The world is the menu. That only works because the content set is small.
sites.typography: Almost no marketing type. Signs in the world carry the words.
sites.performance: The whole site is the scene. Honest about that cost.
sites.mobile: Driving is a desktop fantasy. Touch gets a list, which is the right fallback.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Being inside is the feeling. Driving is not the interface for 120 lessons. Keep links.

sites.name: Three.js Journey
sites.interaction: Lessons are watched and coded. The marketing site is a door, not the classroom.
sites.motion: The island and the lessons do not share one animation clock.
sites.space: A small island sells the course. Lessons are video plus text.
sites.storytelling: Progress through a curriculum is the plot, told plainly once you are in.
sites.navigation: Buy, login, lesson list. Ordinary on purpose after the door.
sites.typography: Course marketing type, then instructional type.
sites.technology: Three.js for the island. Video for the teaching.
sites.performance: The island is one route. Lessons are lighter.
sites.mobile: You cannot learn GLSL from a phone-sized island. The lesson player matters more.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Home may be a world. A lesson must be a lesson. That split is the route map.

sites.name: Merci Michel
sites.interaction: Editorial craft: you read, then you notice the motion.
sites.motion: Soft, precise, rarely spectacular for its own sake.
sites.space: Shallow depth. Paper and screen, not a vista.
sites.storytelling: Culture and craft stories. The reading is the point.
sites.navigation: A studio index you can scan.
sites.typography: Editorial serif and grotesque, carefully set.
sites.technology: High-end front-end, often GSAP, not always a canvas.
sites.performance: Lighter than a game. Still easy to over-animate the reading.
sites.mobile: Type has to reflow. Motion that depends on a desktop line length breaks.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Calm is allowed. Our Wisdom state should feel closer to this than to a race film.

sites.name: Basement
sites.interaction: Type gets in your way on purpose. You push through it.
sites.space: Flat, graphic, sometimes a WebGL accent. The type is the space.
sites.storytelling: A studio personality. Not a curriculum.
sites.navigation: Standard links hiding under maximal type.
sites.typography: The whole page is a type specimen.
sites.technology: Next.js era marketing sites, heavy motion.
sites.performance: Can be cheap to render if it is DOM. Becomes expensive when every glyph is a layer.
sites.mobile: Giant type overflows small screens unless the composition is redesigned.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Type can be the interface. Do not inherit the chaos. Our words move a few baselines, then stop so they can be read.

sites.name: Obys
sites.interaction: Smooth scroll makes the page feel heavy and expensive.
sites.motion: Large type translates and tracks. The motion is the layout.
sites.storytelling: Agency credibility via taste, not via a story.
sites.navigation: A menu of projects. The smooth scroll is the signature, not the IA.
sites.technology: Custom smooth scroll plus GSAP, widely copied.
sites.performance: Smooth scroll fights the platform scroll and the find-in-page mental model.
sites.mobile: Momentum scrolling on iOS plus a second smooth-scroll is carsick.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Scale of type is useful. Lenis-style scroll is not. Native scroll stays.

sites.name: Cuberto
sites.interaction: A custom cursor is the interaction. It changes shape on links.
sites.motion: The cursor animates more than the content.
sites.space: Shallow. The cursor implies a layer above the page.
sites.storytelling: Showreel. You came to see motion.
sites.navigation: Hidden behind the cursor metaphor. You learn the cursor before the sitemap.
sites.typography: Clean grotesk, often masked by the cursor.
sites.performance: A cursor layer is cheap until it is hit-testing the whole document on move.
sites.mobile: There is no cursor. The signature disappears, which means it was never the product.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Do not replace the OS cursor. A halo that yields to touch is the whole pointer spec.

sites.name: Locomotive
sites.interaction: Horizontal sections and smooth scroll are the gesture.
sites.motion: Panels slide laterally. Vertical wheel is remapped.
sites.space: Frieze-like. You move along a wall.
sites.navigation: Remapped scroll hides 'how far' and fights the scrollbar.
sites.performance: Scroll-jacking is a support cost. We will not own the user's wheel.
sites.mobile: Horizontal sections become a trap on a phone unless rewritten as a list.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Keep vertical scroll. Let the vertical position change the world instead of remapping the wheel.

sites.name: Igloo
sites.interaction: DOM nodes and WebGL share a scroll. You are not sure which layer you touched.
sites.motion: Text and meshes move on one scrub.
sites.space: Type sits in the same perspective as the scene.
sites.navigation: You scroll. Links are real DOM so they stay links.
sites.typography: HTML type, placed as if it were in the camera.
sites.technology: WebGL plus DOM overlay. A known pattern, not a library we need.
sites.performance: Syncing DOM and camera every frame is the cost. We do it with CSS variables, not by moving React.
sites.mobile: Perspective type gets unreadable under 400px. Our type stays axis-aligned.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Real HTML in front of one scene. Never put the lesson title only inside the canvas.

sites.name: Darkroom Engineering
sites.interaction: Almost none. The site is a proof of restraint.
sites.storytelling: The story is the file size.
sites.navigation: A short page. You finish it.
sites.technology: Lenis, deliberately under a megabyte in public writeups.
sites.performance: This is the performance lesson. Identity does not require a runtime.
sites.mobile: A light page is the mobile strategy.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Weight is a design decision. We did not add Lenis to feel expensive.

sites.name: Studio Freight
sites.interaction: The library is the interaction: it changes how scroll feels.
sites.motion: Inertial smoothing of native scroll position.
sites.navigation: It does not provide navigation. It changes the feel of whatever navigation you have.
sites.performance: A second scroll pipeline. Conflicts with position: sticky math if you are careless.
sites.mobile: iOS already has momentum. Doubling it feels drunk.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Feel is not identity. Sticky-track math stays on native scroll so the world state is the real scroll position.

sites.name: Rive
sites.interaction: The homepage demo is a state machine you can poke.
sites.motion: States, not a single timeline. Inputs drive transitions.
sites.storytelling: The product teaches itself by being used.
sites.navigation: Docs, community, pricing. The toy is the hero, the docs are the product.
sites.typography: Product marketing type around a live file.
sites.performance: Another runtime and another editor. Our states are seven strings.
sites.mobile: The same state machine has to have a static frame.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Steal the idea of a state machine. Do not ship the runtime. CSS and one frame loop already branch on world.

sites.name: Spline
sites.interaction: You orbit a sample scene. Interaction is the pitch.
sites.space: A toy viewport embedded in a marketing page.
sites.navigation: Normal product nav. The scene is a widget.
sites.performance: Embedded scenes get heavy fast. A widget in a page is the failure mode we are leaving.
sites.mobile: The embed often becomes a poster.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A 3D widget next to a headline is exactly the current PR. The scene has to be the page.

sites.name: Apple iPhone
sites.interaction: Scroll scrubs a product film. You do not drag the phone.
sites.motion: Pinned frames. Copy changes while the object stays.
sites.space: One object, large, center. The page is a viewport.
sites.storytelling: Feature chapters: camera, chip, battery. Each chapter is a new shot of the same object.
sites.navigation: A thin global nav. The story is the scroll.
sites.typography: A short claim per chapter. Never a paragraph beside a render in the first screen.
sites.technology: Video sequences plus DOM. Sometimes a canvas. Enormous production.
sites.performance: Video CDNs. We will not encode a film of a lotus.
sites.mobile: They re-edit the film for small screens. They do not scale the desktop comp.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: One subject, camera does the talking, copy is a caption. Procedural geometry instead of a film, because we are not Apple and the subject is not a phone.

sites.name: Apple Vision Pro
sites.interaction: Scroll and a few hotspots. You are not inside a headset demo.
sites.motion: Spatial video language, very slow, very sure.
sites.space: Cinematic. Huge depth cues, little UI.
sites.storytelling: A product introduction with a beginning and an end.
sites.performance: Not reproducible. The lesson is editing, not the codec.
sites.mobile: The film is recomposed. Type size does not carry the desktop frame.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Authored beats. Our seven worlds are the beats we can afford without a film crew.

sites.name: Stripe
sites.interaction: Gradient meshes respond slightly. The rest is a normal product site.
sites.storytelling: A company explanation. Sections are still sections.
sites.navigation: Extremely clear product nav. This part we keep.
sites.technology: CSS, WebGL gradients on some eras of the homepage.
sites.performance: They are fast. The gradient is not the cost.
sites.mobile: The gradient collapses gracefully because the layout never needed it.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Atmosphere without a subject change is still a website. Negative example for the hero. Positive example for the header.

sites.name: Linear
sites.interaction: The product UI is the picture. You are looking at the tool.
sites.space: Shallow. The screenshot is the depth.
sites.storytelling: Speed and craft, told by showing the app.
sites.navigation: Product nav, changelog, docs. Boring and correct.
sites.performance: Fast because it is not a scene.
sites.mobile: The UI shot is redesigned per breakpoint.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Show the system. Our constellation has to be the product shot, not an illustration beside the product shot.

sites.name: Raycast
sites.interaction: A command palette is the metaphor and the demo.
sites.space: A floating panel over a desktop.
sites.navigation: The palette is the wayfinding lesson: search is an instrument.
sites.mobile: The palette is the mobile problem. Search stays a dialog for us.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: The header readout and search are instrumentation. Do not build a fake command bar that hides Learn.

sites.name: Vercel
sites.interaction: Deploy buttons, tabs of frameworks, a dark grid.
sites.storytelling: Ship. The story is the workflow.
sites.navigation: Docs-grade nav. Excellent. The look is now a template.
sites.typography: Geist, which this repo already uses for UI, not for the spectacle.
sites.technology: Next.js, DOM, some WebGL flourishes on campaign pages.
sites.mobile: The grid scales. The flourishes drop.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Developer-site dark mode is the look we are accused of. Geist stays for UI chrome. The world is not a Vercel template.

sites.name: Notion
sites.interaction: A blank page is the hero metaphor.
sites.navigation: Product nav plus a template gallery.
sites.typography: Serif wordmark, sans UI. A useful split we already have.
sites.mobile: The blank page is the mobile hero too.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Void is a blank instrument, not a blank marketing page. Do not stay in Void. Awaken happens on its own.

sites.name: Figma
sites.interaction: Multiplayer cursors are the demo of presence.
sites.performance: The demo is a video so the homepage stays light.
sites.mobile: The video poster is the fallback.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Presence should be felt (pointer drift) without fake multiplayer cursors. One user, one local progress.

sites.name: Framer
sites.interaction: Components animate on the marketing site as samples.
sites.technology: Framer's own runtime on their site.
sites.performance: Easy to ship, easy to look like everyone on the marketplace.
sites.mobile: Templates reflow. Spectacle often does not.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Springs on every block are how you get a template. We use them almost nowhere.

sites.name: Arc
sites.interaction: The browser chrome is the hero.
sites.storytelling: A new way to browse, told as a tour.
sites.navigation: Download is the only action that matters. The tour is long.
sites.mobile: A long tour must be skippable. Our boot already is.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A tour can be the homepage if every beat changes the same object. Arc changes slides. We change state.

sites.name: Pitch
sites.interaction: Decks animate in the hero.
sites.typography: Presentation type, which is a trap for a reading product.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Do not turn the homepage into a deck. Worlds are not slides with titles.

sites.name: Are.na
sites.interaction: Blocks connect. The interaction is collecting and linking.
sites.motion: Almost none. The graph is the motion.
sites.mobile: The connections reflow into a column.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Knowledge is a graph. Eleven phases are the structures. Days are the blocks. Do not draw 120 edges in WebGL.

sites.name: Obsidian
sites.interaction: The graph view is the demo of a vault.
sites.navigation: Download, then the app. The site is not the tool.
sites.technology: DOM marketing, canvas graph in the app.
sites.performance: The marketing site is light. The graph is not the homepage cost.
sites.mobile: The graph is a desktop feature. The phone app is a list.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A hairball of 120 nodes is not a curriculum. Phase nodes plus day dots. The graph lesson is illumination, not density.

sites.name: Cosmos
sites.interaction: You wander a masonry of images.
sites.navigation: Wander is the nav. Bad for 'what is day 14'.
sites.mobile: Masonry collapses to a column and becomes a feed.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Wandering is the opposite of a 120-day order. We can be spatial and still numbered.

sites.name: The Pudding
sites.interaction: You scroll a chart that is the article.
sites.motion: Scrubbed charts. The data moves. The chrome does not.
sites.space: Flat, full width. The chart is the room.
sites.navigation: A list of essays. Inside an essay, scroll is the nav.
sites.typography: The chart labels are the type. Prose is secondary and still real.
sites.performance: They publish a page, not a runtime.
sites.mobile: Charts are redesigned. A desktop scatter is not pinched.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Progress is the dataset. Nodes light because days are complete, not because a caption says so.

sites.name: Distill
sites.interaction: Figures are interactive. You drag a parameter and the diagram updates.
sites.space: Article column. The figure is inset.
sites.performance: Each article pays for its own figure. The shell is light.
sites.mobile: Drag interactions need a tap alternative. They usually have a play button or a static figure.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Lesson pages may be interactive later. They do not get the homepage scene. Explanation beats spectacle once you are reading.

sites.name: Observable
sites.interaction: Cells react. Change an input, the plot changes.
sites.typography: Mono for code, sans for prose.
sites.performance: A notebook is heavier than a lesson. We do not embed one.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: sceneBus is the same idea as a reactive cell: one value, many readers, no React render per frame.

sites.name: MDN
sites.interaction: Search, sidebar, in-page TOC. Interaction is wayfinding.
sites.performance: Extremely fast. The bar for a lesson.
sites.mobile: The sidebar becomes a menu. Content stays first.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A lesson that is slower or louder than MDN has failed, even if the homepage is a world.

sites.name: Stripe Docs
sites.interaction: Code samples you switch between languages. Copy button.
sites.storytelling: Task-based. You came to do one thing.
sites.mobile: Columns collapse in a known order. Content, then nav.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: /learn keeps a list and a current day. Immersion does not remove the table of contents.

sites.name: Khan Academy
sites.interaction: Mastery rings and a subject map. You press the next exercise.
sites.motion: Small rewards. The map does not fly.
sites.space: A map of subjects, then a worksheet.
sites.navigation: The next exercise is always obvious.
sites.performance: Built for low-end machines. A moral example.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: The next lesson is always one tap away. Our header CTA and the lock both resolve continue. The world does not hide them.

sites.name: Duolingo
sites.interaction: A path of nodes. Tap the current one.
sites.motion: The owl and the path celebrate.
sites.mobile: The path is the mobile home.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A path of nodes is right. A mascot and a fake streak are not. Illumination comes from local completions only.

sites.name: Brilliant
sites.interaction: You answer inside the lesson. The marketing site is ordinary.
sites.motion: Feedback on the answer, not on the scroll.
sites.performance: Lesson weight is the question, not a scene.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Put interaction where the learning is. Homepage spectacle, lesson focus. Do not invert that.

sites.name: Frontend Masters
sites.interaction: A catalogue. Filters, progress, play.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Catalogue density belongs on /learn, not in the first viewport.

sites.name: New York Times Snow Fall
sites.interaction: Scroll reveals the story. There is nothing else to do.
sites.motion: Video and parallax at chapter breaks, then the text resumes.
sites.space: A long article that occasionally opens into a scene.
sites.navigation: The scrollbar is the table of contents.
sites.typography: News serif. The reading column is sacred.
sites.performance: Heavy media was the criticism then and the lesson now.
sites.mobile: The piece was painful on phones. Later NYT work learned.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Open the world at chapter breaks, then let the reader read. Signal releases into the lock. Lessons do not stay inside the scene.

sites.name: The Washington Post
sites.interaction: Graphics you scroll through inside articles.
sites.motion: Stepped reveals tied to the copy.
sites.performance: Graphics are lazy-loaded because the article is long.
sites.mobile: Graphics get a static fallback. They have to.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A long page can change mode. Our mode change is the world index, not a new graphic per section.

sites.name: The Guardian
sites.interaction: Interactives are embedded. The page is still a newspaper.
sites.performance: The newspaper must be fast. Interactives are opt-in weight.
sites.mobile: Embeds often fail. The article survives.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: WebGL is opt-in weight on one route. The rest of the site must survive without it. It does.

sites.name: Reuters Graphics
sites.interaction: Scrubbers and maps.
sites.navigation: The graphic has its own small UI.
sites.typography: Labels, not headlines, do the work.
sites.performance: They ship a graphic, not a framework.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A phase is a question with a visual answer, not a card of text.

sites.name: ProPublica
sites.interaction: Databases you search inside a story.
sites.navigation: Search is the interaction that matters.
sites.performance: The tool has to be fast or the story fails.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Search is already a dialog. Do not bury it in the scene. People come to find a lesson.

sites.name: FiveThirtyEight
sites.interaction: Charts you can read without interacting. Interaction is optional.
sites.typography: Their famous charts are the typography.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: The constellation has to be readable with no hover. Hover adds the name. It does not unlock the meaning.

sites.name: Mapbox
sites.interaction: A map you pan.
sites.navigation: Product nav over a map, which fights the map.
sites.mobile: Touch pan is native to maps and hostile to page scroll.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Do not put a map under a page. Our pan is the camera inside a sticky viewport, and the page scroll is what drives it.

sites.name: Google Earth
sites.interaction: Fly. Search a place. The UI is a globe.
sites.navigation: The globe is the nav. Chrome is minimal.
sites.technology: A full application, not a page.
sites.performance: This is an app weight. Out of scope.
sites.mobile: Touch flight is a different product.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A world you fly is Bruno's lesson again. We are a page with one camera path, not an app.

sites.name: Shadertoy
sites.interaction: You edit a shader or just watch.
sites.motion: The fragment shader is the motion.
sites.space: A fullscreen quad. Depth is faked in the shader.
sites.typography: None on the canvas. UI is the site chrome.
sites.performance: A fullscreen shader can melt a phone. Ours is a tiny seed shader.
sites.mobile: Many shaders are unusable on mobile GPUs.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: One small shader on the seed for life. Not a fullscreen effect, not a gallery.

sites.name: p5.js
sites.interaction: Sketches in the page. The editor is the product.
sites.performance: Examples are sandboxed so one sketch does not sink the docs.
sites.mobile: The editor is the hard part.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Do not embed a creative-coding playground. The world is fixed and authored.

sites.name: Processing
sites.interaction: Exhibition of sketches, then a reference.
sites.technology: Java historically, p5 in the browser.
sites.performance: The site is light. The sketches are not the homepage.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Generative art is a reference, not our brand. Geometry is symbolic and stable.

sites.name: OpenProcessing
sites.interaction: You fork a sketch.
sites.performance: Autoplay canvases are a battery problem. We pause offscreen.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Offscreen pause is mandatory. Autoplay sound is forbidden. We already do both.

sites.name: Refik Anadol
sites.interaction: You watch a data sculpture.
sites.space: A volume of particles that looks like a dream of a dataset.
sites.storytelling: The dataset is the plaque on the wall.
sites.technology: Custom GPU work, often prerecorded for the web.
sites.performance: The real piece is an installation. The site is a record.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Fluid data fog reads as generic AI art. Rejected. Particles stay sparse and geometric.

sites.name: teamLab
sites.interaction: You walk. The work responds to bodies.
sites.space: A room. The architecture is the frame.
sites.technology: Sensors, projectors. The website is a brochure for that.
sites.mobile: The website cannot be the room. Do not pretend.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: One composition, not stacked cards. The web version is a sticky viewport, not a warehouse of projections.

sites.name: Barbican
sites.interaction: Tickets, dates, a calendar. The art is in the building.
sites.performance: Must be fast. It is a public building.
sites.mobile: Tickets on a phone are the job.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Culture can be calm and still modern. We are not an institution and we do not need their chrome. We need their clarity of 'what is on'.

sites.name: Meow Wolf
sites.interaction: You buy a ticket to a narrative maze.
sites.mobile: The maze is not the phone site.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A maze hides the exit. A curriculum must not. Reject thematic overload.

sites.name: Nike
sites.interaction: Shop. The campaign film is seasoning.
sites.motion: Video-led campaigns, product UI is still.
sites.navigation: Shop navigation is sacred. The film never blocks the product grid.
sites.technology: Video CDN plus a commerce stack.
sites.mobile: The shop is mobile-first. The film is optional.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: The continue card is the product grid. It comes after the film, and it is always there. Do not make people hunt for day one.

sites.name: Aesop
sites.interaction: You shop slowly. Motion is restrained.
sites.storytelling: A point of view, then a bottle.
sites.mobile: The quiet composition is redesigned, not squashed.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Wisdom state: sparse, slow, gold on ink. Calm is a feature. Do not perform luxury with a cursor.

sites.name: Porsche
sites.interaction: Scroll a car. Configure it.
sites.navigation: Models, dealers. The story is optional.
sites.technology: WebGL or video of the car, plus a configurator.
sites.performance: The configurator is the heavy part. The story is a film.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A single engineered object under studio light is the lotus's job. Configuration is the constellation, not a car UI.

sites.name: BMW
sites.interaction: Model stories, then a builder.
sites.technology: Video plus WebGL on flagship pages.
sites.performance: Flagship pages are heavy. The rest of the site is a catalogue.
sites.mobile: They ship a separate mobile story.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Only the homepage is the flagship. /learn is the catalogue. Do not make every route a film.

sites.name: Spotify Wrapped
sites.interaction: A personal story you tap through.
sites.motion: Per-card kinetic type. One year, one design.
sites.space: Cards in a stack. Not a world.
sites.navigation: Tap forward. No sitemap inside the story.
sites.technology: Their design system plus a yearly one-off.
sites.performance: It is a campaign. It ships and dies.
sites.mobile: It is designed for the phone first.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Personal data as the visual is right. We have local progress, not a year of listening. No fake Wrapped. Mastery is a ratio of real lessons.

sites.name: Airbnb
sites.interaction: Search a place. The page is a product.
sites.storytelling: None on the homepage. The trip is the product.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Usability testing beats taste when the task is 'continue'. The lock is allowed to look like a control.

sites.name: SSENSE
sites.interaction: Shop. Editorial is a layer.
sites.typography: Fashion editorial, often awkward on purpose.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Editorial type can be awkward and still serious. Our serif title is allowed to be large. It is not allowed to be the only idea.

sites.name: Kinfolk
sites.interaction: You read.
sites.mobile: The measure narrows. It stays a magazine.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: About should feel closer to an essay than to a team grid. This pass does not restage About. The thesis says so, and the homepage was the failure.

sites.name: Dropbox Brand
sites.interaction: A brand site, not the product. You browse principles.
sites.motion: Illustration systems move as a family.
sites.mobile: The system has a small-screen version because it is a system.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Motion should belong to a family of states, not to individual sections. That is what data-world is for.

sites.name: Epic Games
sites.interaction: A store. The engine site is separate. Campaigns are films.
sites.performance: The store must be fast. Trailers are not on the critical path.
sites.mobile: The store is mobile. The cinematic is not the store.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Store and cinematic are different routes. Learn is the store. Home is the cinematic. Do not merge them into one loud page.

sites.name: Unreal Engine
sites.interaction: Feature films of real-time scenes, then a download.
sites.space: Game space, flattened to a film.
sites.technology: Video. The engine is not in the page.
sites.performance: They do not run Unreal in the homepage. That restraint is the lesson.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Do not run a heavier engine to prove seriousness. three.js is already more than the page used well.

sites.name: Godot
sites.interaction: Download. Docs. A showcase.
sites.navigation: Docs are equal to the homepage.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A tool's dignity does not require a scene. Our scene has to justify itself by changing what the page means.

sites.name: Awwwards
sites.interaction: You vote and browse. The sites are elsewhere.
sites.space: A grid of other people's work.
sites.navigation: Collections, SOTD, SOTY. The index is the value.
sites.typography: Their chrome, not the winners' type.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: An index of effects is how the last research failed. We take principles from winners, not their thumbnails.

sites.name: FWA
sites.interaction: Hall of fame. You leave to see the work.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: FWA of the year has been playable work (Bruno Simon, 2025). Playable is a choice we reject for a school. The hall of fame still teaches 'one idea'.

sites.name: CSS Design Awards
sites.interaction: You browse awards.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Usability scores on award sites are often the low number. Where Worlds Take Shape's usability sat under its creativity. We will not win a prize by becoming hard to use.

sites.name: Godly
sites.interaction: You filter galleries, including WebGL.
sites.motion: None. The sites you open have the motion.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A screenshot of WebGL is not research. v1's Godly list padded categories. v2 only keeps sites we can describe.

sites.name: Codrops particle cursor
sites.interaction: Demos of cursor trails and distortion. The directory is the URL because individual demo URLs rot.
sites.performance: A trail on pointermove allocates if you are careless. We are not.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Particle cursors are the annoying custom cursor the brief forbids. The halo is a single div.

sites.name: three.js
sites.interaction: Examples you open. The homepage is a sample.
sites.space: A canvas on a docs site.
sites.performance: Examples are heavy one at a time. The docs are not.
sites.mobile: Examples are desktop-first. The docs reflow.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Use the library directly. Drei would hide the camera math we need to own.

sites.name: Messenger by Abeto
sites.interaction: A product story told as a scene, awarded as a developer site in the 2025 annual, not as a feature grid.
sites.motion: The scene carries the explanation. UI motion is secondary.
sites.space: A communications product given a room.
sites.navigation: The award page is an index. The site itself is the work.
sites.technology: WebGL / real-time, as credited in the 2025 Awwwards annual (developer: Messenger / abeto).
sites.mobile: A product story still needs the actual send-a-message path on a phone.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A developer award is not permission to hide the product. Our continue path stays in the header during the scene.

sites.name: BDSN
sites.interaction: School of Motion 2026 list. Experimental studio pages. If the host has moved, the lesson still holds: experimental type is not a syllabus.
sites.navigation: Work index, often hard to parse.
sites.technology: GSAP-family motion, typical of that list.
sites.performance: Type experiments jank when every glyph animates.
sites.mobile: Illegible type is not a mobile design.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Illegible on purpose is a studio luxury. Our h1 must be readable at first paint.

sites.name: Illoca
sites.interaction: Unseen's AI-native design tool. The launch site is a product, not a case-study PDF.
sites.motion: GSAP, ScrollTrigger, SplitText, CustomEase, per Unseen's note.
sites.storytelling: A funding launch ($13m seed, public post) told as a tool you could imagine using.
sites.typography: Brand type that settles into UI type.
sites.performance: A launch can be heavy once. The tool has to be light forever.
sites.mobile: A design tool people will try from a phone.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Launch spectacle, then a tool. Home, then /learn. Illoca is the cleanest recent example of that handoff.

sites.name: Hubtown
sites.interaction: Unseen SOTD, June 2026. A place brand.
sites.technology: Unseen stack, not re-verified line by line.
sites.mobile: A place brand still needs a phone number and a map.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A single-subject film is allowed when the subject is the whole product. Our subject is the path, so the film is the path's geometry, not a skyline.

sites.name: Apple AirPods Max
sites.interaction: Scroll changes the product shot. Materials are the story.
sites.storytelling: Materials, fit, sound. Chapters of one object.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Chapters of one object: seed, rings, net. Not chapters of unrelated cards.

sites.name: Apple Mac
sites.interaction: A family page, not a single-product film. Comparison is the job.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Eleven phases are a lineup. The constellation is that page. The homepage is not. Do not make the first viewport a comparison grid.

sites.name: nextjs.org
sites.interaction: Docs, blog, a showcase. The homepage is a product explanation.
sites.motion: Small, recently more animated, still a document.
sites.navigation: Docs sidebar is the real product.
sites.typography: Geist, which we already use in chrome.
sites.performance: The docs must be fast. This site is built with the same framework and has no excuse.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: We are a Next app. The framework's own site is still a website. Matching it would miss the brief.

sites.name: React docs
sites.interaction: Interactive examples in the docs. You edit a component and see it.
sites.motion: The example updates. The page does not perform.
sites.space: A document with a live sandboxed figure.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: If a lesson grows an interaction, it should be a figure in the lesson, the way React docs do it, not a background scene.

sites.name: Svelte
sites.interaction: The tutorial is the product. REPL on the left, text on the right, or the reverse.
sites.performance: The REPL is the cost. The marketing page is not.
sites.mobile: The split becomes a stack. The lesson remains doable.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Doing is the interaction that matters in a lesson. Scroll-dolly is the interaction that matters on the homepage. Do not swap them.

sites.name: Tailwind
sites.interaction: You read utility examples. The site itself is restrained.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Utility CSS is how the lock and the header are built. It is not how the world is built. The world is a canvas plus a few state classes.

sites.name: GSAP
sites.interaction: Showcase of other sites. The library site is a brochure for timelines.
sites.motion: Timelines, ScrollTrigger, SplitText. The showcase is other people's work.
sites.performance: The library is small for what it does. The decision is conceptual, not kilobytes alone.
sites.mobile: ScrollTrigger pinning is fiddly on mobile browsers.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A timeline would describe our camera. A scroll-linked function already does, in the same loop as the meshes. A second clock is not bought this pass.

sites.name: Theatre.js
sites.interaction: You scrub a devtools timeline.
sites.space: A scene plus a graph editor.
sites.performance: An editor runtime in production is a dependency we do not want.
sites.mobile: The editor is desktop. The published scene needs a fallback.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Active Theory's craft comes from authored timelines. Our seven states are coarse on purpose so we can author them in code and CSS.

sites.name: Taxi
sites.interaction: It intercepts link clicks and animates the swap.
sites.navigation: It replaces the browser's navigation feel.
sites.performance: It owns the lifecycle of a page. Bugs become 'back is broken'.
sites.mobile: Transitions that assume a desktop width skip content on a phone.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Rejected. History stays native. Continuity is visual (shared type, color, halo), not a transition router.

sites.name: Barba
sites.interaction: Same idea as Taxi, older. PJAX with hooks.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Same rejection. Named so the decision is a comparison, not a vibe.

sites.name: Lenis docs
sites.interaction: You try smoothing on the docs page itself.
sites.space: A normal page that feels heavier.
sites.performance: Sticky sections and smooth scroll disagree unless you virtualise. We did not.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Rejected again, specifically because our world progress is `scroll / (track - viewport)`. Smoothing that number would smear the state machine.

sites.name: React Three Fiber
sites.interaction: Docs for the renderer we use. Examples run a canvas.
sites.storytelling: How to put React on a scene without rerendering per frame.
sites.performance: The docs warn, in practice, that setState in useFrame drops frames. We obeyed.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: The architecture rule is theirs: write the bus from the DOM, read it in useFrame. No per-frame React.

sites.name: Drei
sites.interaction: Helpers: OrbitControls, Text, Environment, ContactShadows.
sites.space: They add objects you did not design.
sites.performance: A large helper surface. We would use a fraction and ship the rest's weight unless tree-shaken carefully.
sites.mobile: OrbitControls on a page fight page scroll. That bug is famous.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Not added. Camera path is the story. OrbitControls would let the user break the story and fight the scrollbar.

sites.name: pmndrs postprocessing
sites.interaction: Bloom, DOF, noise.
sites.mobile: Often the first thing you must disable.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Not added. Bloom would make the lotus prettier and the page more generic. Life comes from the seed shader and the light, which are cheap.

sites.name: Babylon.js
sites.interaction: A playground of engines features.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: We already have three. Switching engines would not change the hero composition.

sites.name: PlayCanvas
sites.interaction: An editor in the browser.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: We are not shipping a game editor. The scene is code, so the state machine stays diffable.

sites.name: PixiJS
sites.interaction: 2D WebGL renderer.
sites.performance: Lighter than a 3D scene. Wrong tool for a camera story.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A camera path needs a perspective camera. 2D would return us to the first canvas experiment, which read as a graphic.

sites.name: Phaser
sites.interaction: A game framework.
sites.performance: A game loop plus our React tree is two apps.
sites.mobile: Games need a different input model.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: The brief says the site should feel like a system, not a game. Phaser would blur that and add weight.

sites.name: Excalidraw
sites.interaction: You draw. The page is the tool.
sites.mobile: Touch drawing works because it was designed for it.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A tool page contains no marketing hero. Our homepage should feel closer to 'you are in the tool' than to 'read about the tool'. The tool is the path, so the path is drawn, not described, in the first viewport.

sites.name: tldraw
sites.interaction: Same family as Excalidraw, more productized.
sites.motion: UI motion of a canvas app.
sites.navigation: Marketing site in front of an app.
sites.mobile: The app is the mobile problem.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Do not put a marketing site in front of the instrument. The instrument is the first viewport. The explanation is the lock.

sites.name: Desmos
sites.interaction: You type a function, the curve moves.
sites.navigation: The expression list is the nav.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Immediate feedback is the standard for a lesson interaction. The homepage's feedback is the world name changing as you scroll, which is the same idea at a coarser grain.

sites.name: GeoGebra
sites.interaction: Constructions you drag.
sites.performance: Applets are heavy. We do not embed one.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Drag-a-point belongs in a lesson about a concept, not in the lotus.

sites.name: Ncase Trust
sites.interaction: You play a repeated game. The essay is the UI.
sites.motion: The tournament animates because you pressed play.
sites.typography: The essay is the labels on the toy.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Nicky Case is the standard for 'interaction is the argument'. Our argument is the path. Playing the lotus is not the argument.

sites.name: Explorable Explanations
sites.interaction: An index of pieces like Ncase. The index itself is plain.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: The index of explorable explanations is a normal page. The works are not. /learn is allowed to be the index. Home is not.

sites.name: Bret Victor
sites.interaction: Essays you scrub. 'Up and Down the Ladder of Abstraction', 'Inventing on Principle'.
sites.motion: Scrubbing a parameter scrubs the picture.
sites.typography: His own essay type. Untouchable as a style. Readable.
sites.mobile: Scrubbers need a finger-sized hit area. Many of the originals do not. We will not copy that failure.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Direct manipulation of a parameter is the highest form of this medium. We use it for scroll→world, not for a dozen toy sliders.

sites.name: Dynamicland
sites.interaction: A real room. The website is a letter about it.
sites.motion: None on the site. The room is the computer.
sites.navigation: A letter, not a nav maze.
sites.performance: The site is almost nothing. The idea is the weight.
sites.mobile: You cannot visit the room on a phone. The letter still works.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A place can be described calmly. Our About page should aim at that tone later. This pass does not pretend the homepage is Dynamicland.

sites.name: Ink & Switch
sites.interaction: Essays about local-first and malleable software.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Local-first is already our progress model: completions live on the device. The visual must say that, and must not imply an account we do not have.

sites.name: Wikipedia
sites.interaction: You search, then you read. The homepage is a portal.
sites.typography: Serif body. The best reading type on the web, still.
sites.performance: Text is cheap. We should remember that on lesson routes.
sites.mobile: The article is the mobile product.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Reading is a solved interface. Lesson pages stay in that family. Do not 'immerse' a lesson into unreadability.

sites.name: Wolfram Alpha
sites.interaction: You ask, it computes.
sites.technology: A huge backend. The page is a form.
sites.performance: The page is fine. The compute is not our problem.
sites.mobile: The input is the mobile UI.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Computation can be invisible. Our 'intelligence' state is a net, not a fake answer engine.

sites.name: freeCodeCamp
sites.interaction: A curriculum map of certifications, then exercises.
sites.performance: Built for bad networks. A serious bar.
sites.mobile: The whole curriculum is on the phone.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A curriculum map does not need WebGL to be clear. Ours has WebGL only on the front door. The map itself is SVG.

sites.name: The Odin Project
sites.interaction: A path of lessons, very explicit.
sites.mobile: The path is a list on purpose.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: When the constellation is unclear, the list must still exist. /learn keeps titles. That is Odin's lesson.

sites.name: boot.dev
sites.interaction: A game-flavored path of programming lessons.
sites.mobile: Designed to be played in a browser, including a laptop on a lap.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Gamification is a neighboring product. We do not add XP, hearts, or a character. Progress is days lit.

sites.name: Scrimba
sites.interaction: The lesson is a recording you can pause and edit.
sites.motion: The IDE and the voice are the motion.
sites.mobile: The player has to work in a narrow window.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Focus mode is the lesson route. Do not put the homepage scene behind a code sample.

sites.name: Exercism
sites.interaction: Mentoring and exercises. Reputation is quiet.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Mentorship is out of scope. The visual of a track is in scope: phases, then days.

sites.name: Advent of Code
sites.interaction: A calendar of 25 days. Each day is a door.
sites.motion: The calendar is the art. ASCII.
sites.technology: HTML that looks like a terminal. Almost no JS.
sites.mobile: The calendar is the mobile page too. It is not pleasant, and that is a choice.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A calendar of days can be the whole identity. Ours is 120, so it cannot be 120 doors in ASCII. It can be 11 structures and a day grid. The restraint of 'almost no JS' is a dare we answer with one scene, not with a framework of motion.

sites.name: LeetCode
sites.interaction: A problem list and an editor.
sites.performance: Too heavy for what it is. Negative example.
sites.mobile: The editor is cramped and still the product.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Density without a world is not seriousness. Do not copy the dashboard.

sites.name: web.dev
sites.interaction: Learn and measure. Lighthouse is the culture.
sites.performance: They will measure us. The scene has to survive that.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Performance is part of the design. Offscreen pause, DPR caps, no second runtime. Stated as a product rule, not a hope.

sites.name: WAI
sites.interaction: Patterns for keyboards, names, motion.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: prefers-reduced-motion is not a courtesy. The still core and the readable lock are the experience for that setting, not a broken version of the film.

sites.name: Inclusive Components
sites.interaction: Patterns: disclosure, tabs, dialog. Written as articles.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Search is a dialog, Explore is a disclosure, the mobile menu is a real set of links. Those patterns stay. The world does not replace them.

sites.name: Josh Comeau
sites.interaction: Interactive figures inside friendly essays. Springs, CSS, React.
sites.motion: The figure moves when you drag the slider he placed.
sites.typography: His own voice, large and readable.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Widget-in-an-essay is the lesson-page future. Not this homepage. Springs are explained by him and still not required for a camera lerp.

sites.name: Emil Kowalski
sites.interaction: Animations that respect feel: duration, easing, interruption.
sites.technology: DOM, often Framer Motion in the demos.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Interruption matters. The boot veil dismisses on pointerdown and keydown. The camera eases toward a target so a fast scroll does not snap.

sites.name: Rauno Freiberg
sites.interaction: Interface craft. Details you feel: press states, blur, light.
sites.space: A personal site, shallow and precise.
sites.mobile: The details survive because they are CSS.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Our micro-interactions should be this small: magnetic link, tilt on the lock, halo. Not a new effect per section.

sites.name: Paco Coursey
sites.interaction: Theme, command menu, craft blog.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A command menu is a power-user layer. We already have search. We do not add a second palette.

sites.name: Material Design
sites.interaction: Guidelines, motion chapter included.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Motion tokens are right. A purple Material hero is the generic AI look we were told to avoid. Our tokens stay ink, cream, gold, signal.

sites.name: Carbon
sites.interaction: IBM's system. Product UI, dense.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Enterprise density is the projects route's cousin (artifacts, metadata) and the homepage's enemy.

sites.name: Polaris
sites.interaction: Admin UI guidelines.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Admin cards are why the homepage felt like SaaS. Cards remain only where a task needs a boundary: the continue lock, a lesson header.

sites.name: Apple HIG
sites.interaction: Motion, depth, and deference are specified.
sites.motion: They tell you when not to move.
sites.typography: San Francisco in the spec. We do not imitate it.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Deference: motion gets out of the way of reading. Signal releases the scene. Lessons do not animate behind the prose.

sites.name: Laws of UX
sites.interaction: One law per page. Jakob, Fitts, Hick, aesthetic-usability.
sites.space: A card per law, which is ironic.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Fitts: the continue control must be a real target, in the header and again in the lock. Hick: do not offer 120 equal choices in the hero.

sites.name: Nielsen Norman
sites.interaction: Articles about users. No spectacle.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Aesthetic-usability will make a pretty broken nav feel acceptable. That is the failure mode of award sites. Our nav stays obvious.

sites.name: Smashing Magazine
sites.interaction: Long articles, a conference, a shop.
sites.performance: Heavy with ads and images. Negative performance example.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: An editorial magazine is what the review said we still were. The first viewport is no longer a magazine cover with an illustration.

sites.name: A List Apart
sites.interaction: Essays.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: About and lessons can be essays. The homepage cannot be an essay with a picture.

sites.name: CSS-Tricks
sites.interaction: Almanac and articles. A reference that became a magazine.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: The almanac idea (a stable reference beside the magazine) is /learn beside the homepage.

sites.name: Practical Typography
sites.interaction: Butterick's book, on one long page. You read.
sites.navigation: The page is the book. Headings are the nav.
sites.mobile: The column narrows. It is still the book.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Type that moves must become type that sits. After the state change, the words hold still long enough to read. A book is the reminder.

sites.name: Google Fonts
sites.interaction: You try a sentence in a face.
sites.motion: The sample reflows as you type.
sites.performance: Font files are the cost. We already loaded Geist and Instrument Serif. We do not add another display family for the effect.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: No new typeface. The kinetic system uses the serif we have, as words, not as a specimen grid.

sites.name: Instrument Serif specimen
sites.interaction: A face designed for editorial display.
sites.mobile: It stays readable at our sizes.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: The h1 uses it because it is already the brand, not because a specimen site told us to animate serifs.

sites.name: Inter
sites.interaction: A UI face, documented obsessively.
sites.space: A specimen page that is also a proof.
sites.storytelling: A design story of a typeface.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: UI chrome stays a grotesque (Geist). Display stays serif. Mixing them is the typographic system. Do not set the world readout in the serif.

sites.name: View Transitions API
sites.interaction: The platform can animate between DOM states.
sites.navigation: It can run on navigations in supporting browsers.
sites.performance: Cheap when it is just opacity. Dangerous when it delays navigation.
sites.mobile: Support is uneven. A fallback is 'no animation', which is fine.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Not used for route changes this pass. A half-supported navigation animation is worse than a reliable native load. Shared identity carries the continuity.

sites.name: Scroll-driven animations
sites.interaction: CSS can bind an animation to scroll.
sites.typography: It can move type without JS.
sites.performance: Cheaper than a scroll listener for style. Our scroll listener also feeds WebGL, so it stays.
sites.mobile: Support is not universal enough to be the only path.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: World state is JS because the canvas needs the same number. CSS only reacts to data-world. We do not maintain two scroll systems.

sites.name: prefers-reduced-motion
sites.interaction: A user setting, not a site.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: We honor it by not starting the loop. The content does not depend on the loop. That is the whole contract.

sites.name: NASA Eyes
sites.interaction: You fly a model of a mission.
sites.performance: An app, not a page. Too much for a homepage.
sites.mobile: A simplified mode exists because it has to.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Literal space is the wrong metaphor (we are not a planetarium) and the right technical warning (a full sim is a product of its own).

sites.name: Gapminder
sites.interaction: Bubbles you play over time. Rosling's chart.
sites.mobile: The tool is usable, not pretty.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Time scrubbing a dataset is scroll scrubbing our world. The difference: our axis is narrative state, not years, and we do not pretend to be a chart of the industry.

sites.name: Our World in Data
sites.interaction: Charts in articles. You can change the country.
sites.performance: Charts are lazy and the prose is fast.
sites.mobile: Charts get a share image and a simple view.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Search plus a clear topic list is the standard for /learn. We already have search. Do not replace it with the constellation.

sites.name: FlowingData
sites.interaction: Nathan Yau's essays. The chart is explained.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A picture that needs a paragraph under it is a caption, not a system. Our picture changes so the paragraph can wait until the lock.

sites.name: D3
sites.interaction: Examples of bindings from data to DOM.
sites.performance: Fine for SVG. Our constellation is already SVG without D3, which keeps the lesson map free of a visualization runtime.
sites.mobile: SVG reflows if you let it.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Do not add D3 for eleven nodes. The map is geometry we control. D3 would be a template of its own.

sites.name: deck.gl
sites.interaction: Large geospatial layers on a map.
sites.performance: Made for millions of points. We have 120 days. Wrong scale.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Instancing millions of points is a solution to a problem we do not have. 380 particles is the budget.

sites.name: Kepler.gl
sites.interaction: A GUI on deck.gl.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A data app is not a school. Mentioned so we do not 'upgrade' the constellation into a BI tool.

sites.name: Cesium
sites.interaction: A globe.
sites.navigation: A product site plus a viewer.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Another globe we will not embed. Same lesson as Google Earth, different vendor, so it is a decision and not a grudge.

sites.name: Felt
sites.interaction: A collaborative map.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Collaboration features imply accounts. We do not have accounts in this experience. Progress stays local. Do not draw other people's cursors.

sites.name: SvelteKit docs
sites.interaction: Tutorial-quality docs.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Different from the Svelte homepage row: this is the IA lesson. A sidebar of lessons beats a spatial menu once you are studying.

sites.name: Astro
sites.interaction: Content sites, islands of interactivity.
sites.performance: The pitch is shipping less JS. We should hear it.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Islands: the scene is one island, dynamic-imported. The lock, the map, and the header are not inside the canvas. That is the architecture, named after a real idea, implemented without adopting Astro (we are already on Next).

sites.name: Remix
sites.interaction: Web fundamentals as the pitch.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Native navigation is a feature. Our refusal of Taxi is the Remix lesson applied to transitions.

sites.name: Vue docs
sites.interaction: A guide you can read in order.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A guide has an order. 120 days have an order. The constellation may be spatial, but the order is numeric and visible.

sites.name: MDN Learn WebGL
sites.interaction: The raw API, which we do not write by hand.
sites.performance: The page is light. The API is easy to misuse.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: We use three.js so we do not hand-write a context. We still own the frame loop. No abstraction above r3f.

sites.name: WebGPU
sites.interaction: A spec, not a site.
sites.performance: Not universally available. A second backend.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Not used. A spec is not a visual idea. three.js WebGL is the path that actually runs for the students.

sites.name: Can I use: WebGL
sites.interaction: A support table.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: WebGL is widespread enough to be the enhancement. The fallback is StillCore, not a prompt to switch browsers.

sites.name: Safari smooth scroll bugs
sites.interaction: A bug tracker, not an inspiration site. Named because sticky and smooth-scroll bugs live here.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Sticky 100svh is tested, not assumed. If the instrument traps scroll on a phone, the track gets shorter. The bug tracker is the reason, not a visual reference.

sites.name: Lighthouse
sites.interaction: A scoring tool.
sites.performance: It will punish a huge JS bundle and a long main thread.
sites.mobile: Mobile throttling is the score that matters.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: The scene is dynamically imported so the lesson routes do not pay for three.js. That split is the Lighthouse decision.

sites.name: Core Web Vitals
sites.interaction: LCP, INP, CLS. A definition.
sites.motion: INP hates long tasks on pointer move.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Pointer move only writes two floats. It does not measure layout. CLS: the title is visible before JS, so data-world must not collapse the heading.

sites.name: Firefox
sites.interaction: A browser homepage. Privacy as the story.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Not a visual reference. A compatibility target. The scene uses ordinary WebGL, not a Chrome-only extension.

sites.name: Chrome experiments
sites.interaction: A gallery of experiments, many abandoned.
sites.performance: The gallery is light. The experiments are not, and many are dead.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: An experiment that dies is not a product. Our scene has a fallback and a content site underneath. That is the difference.

sites.name: Experiments with Google: WebGL
sites.interaction: A filtered gallery.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Filtering a gallery by technology is how you get a monoculture. We did not collect 200 WebGL demos. The set mixes docs, brands, and tools so the lessons conflict, which is the point.

sites.name: A-Frame
sites.interaction: VR in the browser via HTML tags.
sites.space: A headset or a magic window.
sites.performance: VR is a different product and a different performance budget.
sites.mobile: Magic window is a bad page.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Not VR. A homepage people scroll. Putting the curriculum in a headset is a different company.

sites.name: 8th Wall
sites.interaction: AR in the browser, historically.
sites.motion: Camera of the phone as the scene.
sites.typography: Minimal, because the camera is the background.
sites.technology: Their runtime, plus an app install in many cases.
sites.mobile: This is the mobile-native version of WebGL, and it asks for the camera. We will not.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: No camera permission, no AR, no 'point your phone at nothing'. Deviceorientation, if present, is a tiny parallax without a prompt.

sites.name: Zapworks
sites.interaction: Another AR campaign tool.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Same rejection as 8th Wall, second vendor, so it is a category decision: AR is not the system.

sites.name: Spline examples
sites.interaction: The editor, as opposed to the marketing site already listed.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A 3D editor on the homepage would be a toy. The scene is not editable. It is authored.

sites.name: Rive community
sites.interaction: A feed of state machines.
sites.performance: Autoplay of many files. We do not do this.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A feed of animations is the opposite of one authored state machine. One world, seven states.

sites.name: Lottie files
sites.interaction: JSON animations, often exported from After Effects.
sites.performance: Fine for icons. Wrong for a camera.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: The seed is not a Lottie. It has to respond to scroll and mastery, which a baked file does not know about.

sites.name: Lordicon
sites.interaction: Animated icons.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Icon animation will not save a landing page. Not used.

sites.name: Haikei
sites.interaction: You generate SVG backgrounds.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Blob backgrounds are the generic AI/SaaS texture. Rejected. Geometry is hard-edged and few.

sites.name: Mesh gradients
sites.interaction: A generator of the Stripe-like gradient.
sites.performance: An image is cheap and looks like everyone.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: No mesh-gradient hero. The field is dark and the color comes from three lights.

sites.name: Coolors
sites.interaction: A palette generator.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: The palette is already chosen (ink, cream, gold, circuit, signal). Generating a new one per visit would break the brand. Not a reference we follow. A warning.

sites.name: Realtime Colors
sites.interaction: You preview a UI in a palette.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Previewing type on a background is the job of the lower-third title. Cream on ink is the test. Gold is not used for paragraphs.

sites.name: Typescale
sites.interaction: A modular scale calculator.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: The title uses a clamp, not a modular-scale toy. The scale jumps once, from the instrument title to the section h2, so the hierarchy is obvious.

sites.name: Butterick practical page
sites.interaction: The summary of his rules. One page.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Line length on the lock and on lessons stays in a readable measure. The instrument title is allowed to break the measure because it is a title, not a paragraph. The paragraph moved.

sites.name: GOV.UK
sites.interaction: A service. Start now. No brand film.
sites.navigation: Start pages. The best nav pattern in public service.
sites.performance: Fast, accessible, the real performance prize.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: When we worry the world is too strange, GOV.UK is the counterweight: the task ('continue') is labeled in words, in the header, every route.

sites.name: NHS digital services
sites.interaction: A service manual. Patterns for forms and health.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: We are not a health service. The lesson we take is procedural: write the pattern down (this doc) before building it, and do not decorate a task.

sites.name: GOV.UK Design System
sites.interaction: Components with research behind them.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Buttons look like buttons. The enter link and the continue CTA are recognizable. We do not invent a glyph-only start control.

sites.name: USWDS
sites.interaction: The US web design system.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Another public-service system. Same lesson as GOV.UK, included because copying one government site would be folklore. The principle is shared: task first.

sites.name: Baymard
sites.interaction: Checkout research. Huge and paid. The public articles are enough.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: The continue control is a checkout in miniature: one primary action, a clear state (today, now, waiting). Do not offer three competing CTAs in the hero. We offer one in the header and one in the lock.

sites.name: Shopify
sites.interaction: A store builder's marketing site. Sections, logos, a CTA.
sites.mobile: The CTA is the mobile hero.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: This is the template the review is rejecting, even when it is well made. If our first viewport could be swapped for Shopify's, we failed.

sites.name: Webflow
sites.interaction: A site builder. The homepage is a showcase of sites you could build.
sites.motion: Marketing motion, often the template everyone then clones.
sites.technology: Their CMS and, on customer sites, interactions.
sites.performance: The homepage is heavy with video.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Lando was built in Webflow and does not look like Webflow. The tool is not the look. We are not in Webflow. The warning is: interactions panels produce the stagger-fade we banned.

sites.name: Framer gallery
sites.interaction: Templates.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: If a screenshot of our hero could sit in this gallery unlabeled, we failed. The gallery is the anti-pattern board.

sites.name: Awwwards SOTY archive
sites.interaction: The list fetched in v1. Real index of winners.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: The index was real. The per-site technique fields written from it were not. v2 does not auto-fill a winner with a category sentence.

sites.name: School of Motion 2026 list
sites.interaction: An article naming Epic, BDSN, Dropbox Brand, Eszter Bial, Apple, Unseen, Rive, Lusion, Uncommon, Active Theory.
sites.motion: The article discusses editing, not a single effect.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Use the article as a reading list. Do not generate one JSON row per named site by pasting the same 'great animation' sentence. The ones we can describe have their own rows.

sites.name: Uncommon
sites.interaction: A studio site that has to be the portfolio piece, not a grid of thumbnails.
sites.technology: Next.js, GSAP, and Strapi, per Hon Tran's public case study of the studio site.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Hon Tran's note on Uncommon: the studio site has to be the work. Ours has the same problem. A landing card beside a lotus fails it. The first viewport is the system.

sites.name: Colorlib animation roundup
sites.interaction: The v1 fetch that actually named stacks (Lando's Webflow+GSAP+three+Rive+Lenis+Taxi).
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Stacks from this article are usable facts. Adjectives from this article are not. Lando's row uses the stack and the described frames, not the listicle's enthusiasm.

sites.name: Hon Tran juror note
sites.interaction: A juror's essay: art direction and directed motion, around 60fps, matter more than the stack.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: 60fps of an undifferentiated lotus is still a landing page. Direction is the state machine. The stack is whatever holds 60fps. If the URL is only his studio and not the essay, the lesson is still the one recorded in v1 from the fetch, not a new invention.

sites.name: Utsubo Three.js 2026
sites.interaction: Their essay's useful line, from the v1 fetch: one idea per site, and WebGPU is not automatic.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: One idea: a learning path as a single instrument. WebGPU stays off.

sites.name: Active Theory work index
sites.interaction: The URL the brief named. The previous fetch returned no project HTML.
sites.storytelling: Their work page is supposed to be the index of rooms.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Do not describe projects we did not see. The Active Theory lesson used in the product comes from the public record of how they work (one idea, Theatre, fallbacks), not from a scraped grid.

sites.name: Codrops kinetic type
sites.interaction: Demos that throw glyphs around.
sites.performance: Splitting into spans is cheap until it is every paragraph, and it is hostile to translation and to screen readers if done wrong.
sites.mobile: Per-character motion is noise on a phone.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: We split words, not characters. The words are the accessible name. Codrops is the temptation we did not take.

sites.name: Apple product accessibility
sites.interaction: A marketing page about access. The existence of the page is the lesson.
sites.mobile: The page is about the phone.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Reduced motion, keyboard, and readable text are features we ship, not a footer link. The still core is part of the product.

sites.name: Android accessibility
sites.interaction: Touch target guidance. 48dp is the spirit.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Day dots are wrapped in at least 32px targets (we use min-h-8). Phase controls are buttons. The new enter link is min-height 44px.

sites.name: iOS Human Interface, motion
sites.interaction: Motion should be purposeful, optional, and short.
sites.mobile: Reduce Motion is a system setting.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Our boot is under three seconds and skippable. Camera motion eases and stays small. We do not loop a cinematic forever in the background of a lesson.

sites.name: Material motion
sites.interaction: Easing tokens, duration tokens, container transform.
sites.performance: Container transform is a navigation pattern.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A shared-element morph from lotus to constellation would be the elegant version. We do not fake it across routes. The shared element is conceptual (eleven nodes), not a View Transition.

sites.name: IBM motion
sites.interaction: Productive motion versus expressive motion. They separate them.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Homepage is expressive (the world). Lock, header, lesson are productive (short, functional). Carbon's split is the permission structure.

sites.name: Salesforce Lightning
sites.interaction: Enterprise components. Cards, everywhere.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: If the homepage starts to look like Lightning, stop. The card grid is the enemy named in the brief.

sites.name: Atlassian Design
sites.interaction: Same family. Dense product UI.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Projects can borrow artifact metadata (quiet, technical). The homepage cannot borrow a Jira board.

sites.name: GitHub
sites.interaction: A tool. The homepage is now a product pitch, the app is a forge.
sites.navigation: Repos, issues, PRs. The best IA we actually use every day.
sites.performance: The app is fast enough to live in.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: This repository is the product's source. The website should not look like github.com, and the workflow (branch, PR, no merge to main) is not a visual reference. It is how this change ships.

sites.name: Duolingo path details
sites.interaction: The in-app path, as opposed to the marketing site.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A winding path of every day is legible for a language app and noisy for 120 engineering lessons. We group by phase. The winding path is the idea we scaled up, not the drawing we copied.

sites.name: Anki
sites.interaction: Spaced repetition. The web is plain. The algorithm is the product.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: We do not claim spaced repetition we do not run. Completing a day lights a node. That is the whole learning science we are allowed to visualize.

sites.name: Readwise
sites.interaction: Highlights resurfaced.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Resurfacing is not our feature. Do not add a 'daily quote' widget to feel wise.

sites.name: Blinkist
sites.interaction: Summaries. Marketing is a library of covers.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: We are not a summary product. The 120 days are the work, not a 15-minute substitute. The visual should feel like a practice, not a shelf of covers.

sites.name: MasterClass
sites.interaction: Celebrity teachers, trailers, a dark cinematic homepage.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Dark plus a trailer plus a famous face is the guru trap in commercial form. No trailer, no face, no 'learn from the master' hero.

sites.name: Coursera
sites.interaction: A catalogue of universities.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A catalogue homepage is the other failure mode (opposite of MasterClass). We are neither a trailer nor a course grid in the first viewport.

sites.name: edX
sites.interaction: Same catalogue shape as Coursera.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Included so Coursera is not a strawman. Catalogue-first is a category, and it is not the first viewport. It is /learn.

sites.name: Udacity
sites.interaction: Nanodegree marketing. Career outcomes, logos.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Do not lead with a salary claim or a logo wall. Outcomes live on the lesson, in the lock, as that day's outcomes, which already exist in the data.

sites.name: DeepLearning.AI
sites.interaction: Andrew Ng's courses. A face, a catalogue.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A face as the brand is the guru problem with a Stanford halo. THE AI RISHI is a practice, not a portrait.

sites.name: fast.ai
sites.interaction: A course that starts coding immediately. The site is plain.
sites.mobile: The lessons are the mobile experience.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Plain and serious can coexist with a theatrical front door, only if the lessons stay this plain. They do.

sites.name: Full Stack Open
sites.interaction: A free university course, one long site.
sites.technology: Gatsby-class, the content is the point.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: A course can be a book. Our lessons are closer to this than to the homepage. The homepage is the cover, and the cover is now an instrument rather than a blurb.

sites.name: OSSU
sites.interaction: A curriculum as a README.
sites.mobile: A README on a phone is a long scroll.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: The curriculum is data (phases, days, published flags). The visual is a view of that data. A README is the honest fallback, and /learn is that fallback, designed.

sites.name: Teach Yourself Computer Science
sites.interaction: One page, a few books per area. Opinionated and short.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Restraint in the curriculum copy. We do not add motivational paragraphs to the first viewport to explain the geometry. The geometry, then the lock, then the map.

sites.name: Roadmap.sh
sites.interaction: Interactive roadmaps. Nodes, progress, a popular DevOps map.
sites.performance: The SVG is the cost. It is still cheaper than a scene.
sites.mobile: The map is pinch-awkward. They have a list too.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: The closest product cousin. We do not clone the flowchart. We share the truth: progress ticks nodes. Our nodes are the eleven phases of this programme, not a generic DevOps map, and the first viewport is not the flowchart.

sites.name: Cisco learning
sites.interaction: Packet-tracer flavored course marketing.
sites.lessonForTheAiRishi: Certification portals are the visual this brand must not slide back into. No dashboard of badges in the hero.
